Fig. 2. Overview of the proposed VoxShield framework. A noise generator G produces perturbations that are added to clean 3D medical images to create protected volumes. A surrogate model Fs computes LSPD and L′ seg to drive protected images away from the original decision boundaries. An inter-slice frequency consistency disruption module enforces LISC by maximizing spectral discrepancy between adjacent slices, destroying the volumetric continuity that 3D models rely on.
Table 1. Protection effectiveness on victim 3D UNet. DSC (%) ↓ and HD95 (mm) ↑ indicate stronger protection; PSNR (dB) ↑ and SSIM ↑ measure perturbation imperceptibility. Best UE results in bold.

Fig. 1. The defense mechanism of VoxShield. Left: A model trained on clean data learns coherent volumetric representations and segments accurately on clean test volumes. Right: VoxShield disrupts inter-slice consistency by injecting spectrally diverse perturbations across adjacent slices. Consequently, a model trained on such protected data fails to extract coherent cross-slice features, yielding severely degraded segmentation on clean test inputs.
